highlights.title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
highlights.summary: The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity.
body: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.

The claim, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, is the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity.
The warning has prompted calls to action, with US Senator Bernie Sanders demanding a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.
President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".

highlights.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
highlights.summary: A new feature coming to Slack will allow you to build interactive reports, polls, dashboards, presentations, microsites, and other tools directly inside a chat. With Slackforce Surfaces, you can describe to Slackbot what you need, and it will use AI to gather information from relevant conversations…
body: You can ask Slackbot to build a tool for you by just describing it.

Once Slackbot creates a Surface, you can share it with colleagues and pin it to channels, allowing other people to view it, interact with it, and leave comments. In one example shared by Slack, a user asks Slackbot for help creating an arcade-themed visualization of AI token usage. The AI assistant then generates an interactive dashboard showing token usage across different divisions, such as sales, design, and engineering.

“You’re not exporting your data to some other tool to make sense of it, you’re asking Slackbot to build the dashboard, the deck, the report right where the conversation already is, and your whole team can act on it together,” Ryan Gavin, Slack’s chief marketing officer, tells The Verge in an email.

This update comes just months after Slack overhauled Slackbot to make the tool more like an AI assistant, allowing it to summarize information across channels, sort through messages, and find time to schedule meetings. It also added collaborative vibe coding channels last month.

highlights.title: Star Trek's 3 Versions Of Captain James T. Kirk: The Definitive Ranking
highlights.summary: The easy way to rank the three live-action versions of Kirk would be to simply declare William Shatner the winner and move on. After all, he's the actor who delivered us one of science fiction's most enduring characters.
body: Captain James T. Kirk has been one of television's defining heroes for nearly 60 years. For some fans, he'll always look and sound like William Shatner. Others grew up with Chris Pine's brash, Kelvin Timeline captain. And for a new generation discovering Star Trek through Strange New Worlds, Paul Wesley is steadily making the role his own.

None of the three actors is playing exactly the same man. Shatner established the legend. Pine explored how a different upbringing could shape the same extraordinary leader. Wesley is showing us the ambitious young officer still growing into the captain who would one day command the Enterprise. Together, they give us a fuller picture of the human being sitting in that captain’s chair, flaws and all.
With that in mind, here's how the three live-action versions of Captain James T. Kirk rank.

highlights.title: September’s Collabs Corner: Raiding John Cena in Clash of Clans, Among Us in Subway Surfers, and more
highlights.summary: Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations. Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places.
body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.

Supercell’s Clash of Clans has formed its second tag team with the WWE, bringing six wrestling stars in-game as playable characters. Among them are Cody Rhodes as Barbarian King, The Undertaker as Grand Warden and Alexa Bliss as Archer Queen.

The collaboration sees players join Cody Rhodes on the hunt for John Cena’s in-game village, unlocking exclusive rewards as they seek out his base this month. The more players raid, the higher the chance of locating the elusive locale. There’s even a Cody Rhodes statue to be found.
John Cena, the wrestling giant turned actor, is said to be a long-time player of Clash of Clans.

body: Oasis put on a drone show over their home city to announce their upcoming tour.
A drone formation showed the band's logo and was replaced by the date 14.09.26 and the time 4pm BST [16:00], which is when the announcement expected to happen.
The band, who reunited for the first time since splitting in 2009 for the successful Live '25 tour last year, have been dropping hints about tour venues on social media recently.
Liam and Noel Gallagher discussed their reunion in the new documentary Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger, which was released on Wednesday.

highlights.title: Is AI Actually Going to Kill Us All?
highlights.summary: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we dig into a former Anthropic researcher’s AI doomsday warning, the latest upgrades from Apple’s event, and the census report that claimed Trump won the 2020 election.
body: This week on Uncanny Valley, an AI researcher’s resignation from Anthropic went viral on social media after he claimed there’s a real chance AI could wipe out humanity within a decade. WIRED’s Will Knight joins Brian Barrett and Leah Feiger to assess whether the doom narrative is overblown or overdue. We also discuss Apple’s debut of its $2,000 foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, and the new “always listening” Apple Watch features that have Brian feeling more than a little uneasy. Plus, a WIRED investigation found that the US Census Bureau used faulty data to create a misleading report touted by the Trump administration.

highlights.title: Rybakina denies Gauff to set up blockbuster US Open final with Sabalenka
highlights.summary: American hearts were broken as Elena Rybakina silenced Coco Gauff and the New York crowd to set up a blockbuster US Open final against Aryna Sabalenka, who defeated Jessica Pegula to move a win away from her third straight title at Flushing Meadows.
body: Rybakina battled back to upset home favourite Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 in a fierce semi-final showdown to secure a ​title showdown with defending champion Sabalenka and stay ​on course for a ‌third Grand Slam crown.
Sabalenka had beaten Gauff's American compatriot Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 ‌earlier in the night to close in on a ​rare three-peat in New York.

"Of course there were nerves," admitted Rybakina in her on-court interview. "Coco is a great player. It's always tough to play her. Even if sometimes her first serve doesn't go the second one is so heavy it's difficult to dictate the rallies. I took a deep breath, tried to talk positive with myself and just told myself I need to fight and try to show good tennis."

Gauff absorbed relentless pressure ​but stayed strong to draw errors from the Kazakh, ​breaking in the sixth ⁠game and taking the ⁠opening set in front of a passionate crowd ‌that included former first lady Michelle Obama.

highlights.title: Gary Larson's 10 Best The Far Side Comics, Ranked
highlights.summary: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — and sometimes even just one panel — to express a joke or a sentiment.
body: Yet, we’ve seen it do so much more than that. Characters like Snoopy and Garfield have become part of the fabric of our culture, which means comic strips are capable of greatness. And since greatness is possible, what, then, makes a comic strip great?

The first instinct is to go for something “deep.” Comic strips like Peanuts and Calvin and Hobbes occasionally ventured outside of comedy to examine the world and say something thoughtful about it. But that’s not the case for other comic strips that don’t go deep. For Garfield, I’d argue greatness would come down to a really clever, relatable gag. For something like Prince Valiant, which specialized in highly detailed, picturesque images, I imagine greatness would relate to visual appeal.
So what would the measure of greatness be for Gary Larson’s The Far Side?

highlights.title: August 2026 mobile game charts: Fate/Grand Order’s big anniversary, Valorant Mobile's rise and Brawl Stars’ worst month of the year
highlights.summary: Below you can see the latest top games and companies by downloads and revenue for August 2026, as well as the big stories and trends from the last month. Data is provided by AppMagic. Check out profiles of the world's top publishers in the Top 50 Mobile Game Makers 2025 list.
body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

body: Ah Biao, who was born in Shanxi, China, and is now based in Bangkok, works as a director, screenwriter and cinematographer. “Border” is his first feature, placing him in San Sebastián’s main competition lineup alongside veteran directors Mike Leigh, Pablo Larraín, Nicole Garcia and Yeşim Ustaoğlu.

Borderless Films produced “Border,” with Jenny Man Wu as producer alongside fellow producers Lili Tong, Tyler Hill and Xue Ma. “For us, bringing a fully independently produced first feature to San Sebastián’s official competition is especially meaningful,” said producer Jenny Man Wu. “The film was carried forward by a deeply committed team who believed in Ah Biao’s vision and found ways to sustain it at every stage of its production.”

The film also figures among 24 titles in the running for this year’s Sebastiane Award, an honor Basque LGBTIQA+ association Gehitu gives to the film judged the strongest portrayal of queer lives and experiences.

highlights.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for ricotta, blackberry and lemon cake | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: Make the most of the early-autumn glut of fruit with this quick, squidgy-crumbed bake that’s bursting with berries. Every year, I get annoyed with myself for not making the most of blackberry season, and then it’s gone before I’ve had a chance really to enjoy them.
body: Heat the oven to 180C (160C fan)/350F/gas 4, and grease and line a 23cm loose-bottomed cake tin.

Put the sugar and lemon zest in a bowl and use your fingertips to rub together until fragrant. Add the eggs and oil, whisk until frothy, then mix in the ricotta. Finally, sift in the flour, baking powder and salt, and stir gently to combine.

Pour the batter into the lined tin, scatter the blackberries on top, and bake for 28-32 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Leave the cake to cool completely in its tin, then turn out and dust with icing sugar.
For the whipped ricotta, whisk all the ingredients in a bowl until smooth and creamy; alternatively, for a super-smooth result, blitz it in a food processor.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang explains why Nvidia will grow an astounding 70% next year
highlights.summary: Nvidia has its finger in every pie, and sees another year of plenty in its future, Jensen Huang says. But, he insists, its deals are not circular.
body: Founder, CEO, and tireless Nvidia hype man Jensen Huang told attendees at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology conference on Thursday why his company’s AI domination — and revenues — will continue its record-breaking growth streak through the end of next year.

There’s been endless hand-wringing over whether Nvidia’s party will end as it faces increasing competition for GPUs and AI chips from all directions: the hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, each building their own) and the AI labs (Anthropic and OpenAI, which are building their own), as well as from newly public competitor Cerebras and startups such as Etched.

“Most people think Nvidia builds a chip. I mean, you need airplanes to ship what we build,” Huang said, adding that the company continues to battle a perception from its early days. Nvidia invented the GPU, which back then were largely sold to consumers to improve PC gaming. “One GPU now is not $399. It’s $8.5 million dollars. That’s one GPU, all connected with NVLink, 2 million parts, right? 250,000 kilowatts. That’s a GPU, and we ship thousands of them.”

highlights.title: UK economy defies forecasts with surprise 0.4% growth in July
highlights.summary: Welcome boost for chancellor with unexpected rise put down to rapid growth of AI in services sector outweighing Iran war fallout. The UK economy grew in July as the rapid growth of AI appeared to outweigh the economic damage from the Iran war, in a welcome boost for John Healey before next month’s…
body: The UK economy grew in July as the rapid expansion of AI appeared to outweigh the economic damage from the Iran war, in a welcome boost for John Healey.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed a surprise 0.4% increase in gross domestic product (GDP), compared with 0.3% growth in June. City economists had forecast zero growth.

The figures suggested the economy continued to be robust despite the fallout from the Iran war, which has raised energy costs and led to higher interest rates than were expected at the start of the year.

The ONS said the expansion in July was driven by growth of 0.4% in the services sector, particularly admin services, and computer programming and consulting. Within the latter sector, it said, “many of the businesses reporting the largest turnover in July 2026 are involved in activities related to artificial intelligence and cloud computing”.

highlights.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.
body: Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.
Players have long loved the electricity of playing night matches under the lights in the nation's biggest city.
But the tournament had already set a record with three post-2am finishes over the first six days, as well as having two other matches go past 1am.

highlights.title: 33 Years Later, the Best Sci-Fi Show of the '90s Is Officially Streaming for Free
highlights.summary: Created by Chris Carter, The X-Files is about a pair of FBI agents who investigate cases involving the paranormal — and Carter interpreted “paranormal” very broadly. The agents investigated everything from aliens to urban legends to ghosts to many other strange goings-on.
body: For some decades, it might be a bit tough to determine what the best sci-fi TV show was. The 1960s had both Star Trek and The Twilight Zone, which is a really difficult choice. For the 1970s, Battlestar Galactica probably wins, but it has some competition from Space: 1999 and The Six Million Dollar Man. The 1980s had Star Trek: The Next Generation, but V gives that show a run for its money. In the 1990s, however, one show stands out as the best sci-fi series of the decade without any serious contender — and that show is currently free to stream on Pluto TV.

Mulder was the true believer of the pair. His sister was abducted by aliens when he was a kid and he believed that all kinds of spectacular things were possible. Meanwhile, Scully was the skeptic, a medical doctor with a rigid scientific viewpoint who needed to be convinced of everything. That yin and yang was the genius of The X-Files. It allowed everyone in the audience — the believers and skeptics alike — to identify with at least one of the two main characters.

highlights.title: PixelCon brings international mobile games experts to Bratislava for a free conference
highlights.summary: Slovak game studio Pixel Federation is preparing the first edition of PixelCon, a new mobile games conference designed to connect Central European developers with experienced professionals from some of the world's leading studios, including Rovio, Supercell, Wooga and Electronic Arts.
body: Taking place on September 14th, 2026 in Bratislava, PixelCon is a free, open conference aimed at game developers, students, indie creators and professionals from across the games industry. Registration is required due to limited capacity.

Among the international speakers is Jeremy Widdowson, head of growth at Rovio, bringing experience from one of Europe's best-known mobile games companies, the studio behind the global Angry Birds franchise.

The programme also features Stanislav Stankovič, game design director at Electronic Arts, Maya Hofree, general manager of Hay Day at Supercell, and Florian Blaesche, director of player experience at Wooga, who will share their perspectives on building successful mobile games, player engagement and long-term retention.
The international line-up will be joined by Slovak and Czech industry leaders, including Pixel Federation experts and founders of local studios such as Flyboys, PowerPlay Studio and Impact Games.

highlights.title: The age of tiramisu: a runaway dessert trend – and what it reveals about nostalgia and decadence
highlights.summary: The coffee and cream pudding has always been popular. But now it’s inspired a dedicated cafe and countless products, from drinks to ice-creams to buns. What’s behind this big cultural craving?
body: When Giancarlo Fanigliulo opened Marrone, a cafe dedicated to tiramisu in London’s Soho in August, he hadn’t anticipated he would sell out within two and a half hours. “I was expecting a buzz, but I wasn’t expecting queues around the corner,” he tells me. “It was insane.”

This kind of excitement about the Italian dessert is not a one-off – we are, it seems, living in an age of tiramisu-mania. Nearly all of the high street coffee chains have offered some kind of tiramisu coffee as a seasonal special (in the US, Dunkin’ currently has four different tiramisu-flavoured drinks on its menu). Meanwhile, Haagen-Dazs and Carte D’or now sell tiramisu ice-cream, London chain Buns from Home offers a tiramisu-flavoured croissant-dough bun and social media is awash with tiramisu recipes and videos of “tiramisu drawers” – trays of the dessert ready to serve out of drawers in chefs’ kitchens – as popularised by the viral one at Manchester pasta restaurant Onda.
points: The coffee and cream pudding has always been popular.
But now it’s inspired a dedicated cafe and countless products, from drinks to ice-creams to buns.
When Giancarlo Fanigliulo opened Marrone, a cafe dedicated to tiramisu in London’s Soho in August, he hadn’t anticipated he would sell out within two and a half hours.
“I was expecting a buzz, but I wasn’t expecting queues around the corner,” he tells me.

highlights.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
highlights.summary: César de la Fuente’s lab uses Codex and ChatGPT to search living and extinct genomes for antimicrobial candidates to fight drug-resistant infections.
body: César de la Fuente and his lab probe the genomes of living and extinct organisms for molecules that could help fight drug-resistant infections.

Drug-resistant microbes including bacteria, fungi, parasites, and viruses are a growing global threat. About five million deaths in 2021 were associated ⁠ (opens in a new window) with bacterial antimicrobial resistance—an annual toll projected to roughly double by 2050. It can take years to find molecules with the potential to become antimicrobials. Researchers are using AI to accelerate this early stage of discovery.

“Antimicrobial resistance is one of the greatest existential threats to humanity in my opinion,” said César de la Fuente ⁠ (opens in a new window), a bioengineer whose cross-disciplinary lab searches for antimicrobial candidates. “And yet, we haven’t had a new class of antibiotics for 50 years.”
Much of modern antimicrobial development focuses on modifying existing medicines or searching familiar classes of chemicals. But that approach offers diminishing returns.

highlights.title: Five-set tennis is under attack. Killing it would be a colossal unforced error | Andrew Lawrence
highlights.summary: Five-set matches are physically punishing, occasionally absurd and increasingly under threat. They also produce much of what makes grand slam tennis great. Tuesday night’s quarter-final match between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz had everything a US Open spectacle could ask for: huge stakes…
body: Somewhat predictably, the discourse among media and fans following the late-night match has swiftly moved on from the USTA’s misadventures in scheduling to a referendum on the five-set match and whether it should be put out to pasture. For the record: that would be a colossal unforced error.

Five-setters aren’t just intrinsic to the grand slam canon. They are a badge of honor in the men’s game, confirmation that a player can and did indeed hack it in the big leagues. John Isner may not have won a major during his time on tour. But his capacity for grinding out marathon matches – not least the three-day, 11-hour epic he played against Nicholas Mahut at Wimbledon in 2010 – is why he remains highly respected by peers and fans alike.

Best-of-five is the exclusive framing device for the best matches in history and an imprimatur of the sport’s most revered champions. (See, The Greatest Match Ever Played or last year’s French Open final.) Even the losers are celebrated merely for having survived and played on to become part of the tale. “People still remember this match but he didn’t know if I was the winner,” Mahut said in 2015. “So, maybe, in 10 years people will think I won the match.”
points: Five-set matches are physically punishing, occasionally absurd and increasingly under threat.
They also produce much of what makes grand slam tennis great.
For the record: that would be a colossal unforced error.
“People still remember this match but he didn’t know if I was the winner,” Mahut said in 2015.

highlights.title: 24 Years Later, the 220-Episode Action Classic That Defined a Generation Is Free to Stream on YouTube
highlights.summary: Some anime feel less like TV shows than cultural events woven into the fabric of our childhoods. Dragon Ball Z introduced generations of viewers to the idea that a fight could somehow last 12 episodes and still leave you breathless.
body: One of the greatest among them and a major part of the “ Big Three,” Naruto is the hardest to ignore. The original series, available to stream for free on Pluto TV right now, follows the young Naruto Uzumaki on his quest to become his village’s Hokage, its most respected ninja. His brash, reckless personality makes him prone to trouble, while the Nine-Tailed Fox sealed inside him has made him an outcast among villagers who fear the creature’s power. It’s a volatile combination for a lead, yet it ultimately anchored what would become one of the biggest anime franchises in the world.

At first, Naruto presents itself as a show about ninjas hurling increasingly ridiculous techniques at each other. As the series progresses, it becomes a surprisingly earnest story about loneliness, friendship, perseverance, and the desire to be recognized. For Naruto, becoming Hokage was never really about political ambition or raw power. It was a lonely child's desperate blueprint for survival. For a kid raised on cold stares and averted eyes, that title was the only guaranteed way he could force a village that treated him like a curse to finally acknowledge his existence.
points: Some anime feel less like TV shows than cultural events woven into the fabric of our childhoods.
Dragon Ball Z introduced generations of viewers to the idea that a fight could somehow last 12 episodes and still leave you breathless.

highlights.title: Experience: I’ve visited every motorway service station in Britain
highlights.summary: Some people don’t understand my lifelong enthusiasm for roadside stop-offs – now visiting and cataloguing them is what I do for a living. When I was 10 years old, the highlight of my summer holidays was going to work with my dad, who is a lorry driver.
body: My dad thought stopping was a waste of time, but his designated rest stops were my favourite part of the trip. Depending on the journey, we might stop for two or three meals. I always hoped at least one would be at a Little Chef. I loved their Olympic Breakfast, a massive full English, and every meal was rounded off with a lollipop – what more could a 10-year-old want?

As I got older, motorway services retained their air of magic. In 2012, when I was 14, I found the website motorwayservices.uk, which reviewed lots of major service stations. Any time my family visited one, I’d take pictures and contribute to the site.
I learned to drive as soon as I turned 17 and bought myself a two-door Smart car, which I still drive today. After I passed my test, I’d drive out to services near my home in Bristol.

After leaving school, I got a job as a bus driver, but I soon realised that, while I loved the driving, there wasn’t enough time for stopping. I carried on visiting as many services as I could on my days off, just as a hobby, but soon I decided to try to make this my job.

highlights.title: OpenAI Wants to Know if an AI Industry Slowdown Would Even Be Legal
highlights.summary: AI leaders worry antitrust law could stand in the way of what they view as an increasingly urgent push to coordinate a slowdown in AI development.
body: OpenAI has asked members of Congress in recent weeks for clear guidance about whether orchestrating an industry-wide slowdown on frontier AI development would be legal, people close to the company tell WIRED.
Substantive coordination on safety between AI labs may risk running afoul of antitrust law, the people say, which poses a significant obstacle to bringing major tech giants on board with the effort.

Last weekend, OpenAI’s chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, published a blog post arguing that the best path forward for the AI research world includes “coordinating to slow down future development,” which he thinks will be key to ensuring that self-improving AI systems are safe. In the short term, he expects “ voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established.”

highlights.title: Anthropic details bad actors’ efforts to misuse its AI for bioweapons
highlights.summary: Report comes two days after former employee quit claiming company’s models could cause human extinction by 2030. Criminals, state-sponsored groups, spyware vendors, scientists and propagandists have attempted to use Anthropic’s powerful artificial intelligence models to design missiles and bombs…
body: “The cases we share here aren’t typical misuse, but rather examples of the most notable and novel threat activity we’ve identified to date,” Anthropic wrote in its 154-page report. “We’re publishing this work because we believe we have a responsibility to disclose malicious misuse of our services.”

In particular, the company detailed five case studies of scientists using its AI models in biological research. In these examples, Anthropic said the researchers circumvented its safeguards meant to prevent users from “unsupported regions”, as well as worked to hide the purpose of their work.
“Biological misuse is one of the most serious risks of frontier AI models,” Anthropic wrote. “Without the correct safeguards, such capabilities could have catastrophic consequences.”

Anthropic said it banned these accounts. The company did not reveal the names of the research institutions or the countries where the misuse took place, saying it was uncertain of the researchers’ intent.

highlights.title: Anthropic details distillation campaigns from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and DeepSeek
highlights.summary: A new report released Thursday by Anthropic alleges persistent distillation attacks by China-based AI companies, which have escalated in recent months as competition in the space has intensified.
body: “Over the last several months, unauthorized labs have developed increasingly sophisticated methods to circumvent our defenses and harvest the capabilities of US frontier models,” the report reads. “The campaigns we identified targeted some of Claude’s most valuable capabilities, including agentic capabilities and tool use, coding and data analysis, and logical reasoning.”

Anthropic previously spoke out about distillation attacks in February, even calling out specific labs. OpenAI has reported similar activity, which it attributed to DeepSeek specifically. But the campaigns detailed in Anthropic’s new report are both larger and more aggressive. All told, the company observed nearly 200 million exchanges linked to distillation attacks, attributed to five separate campaigns.

Broadly, distillation attacks focus on extracting the chain of thought from a model’s response to various queries. That chain of thought can then be used to train a smaller model on general reasoning ability through supervised fine-tuning.

Uzbekistan, the host nation, are the favourites to win the 208-team biennial chess Olympiad in Samarkand, which has its opening ceremony on Tuesday, and its first round (of 11) on Wednesday.
body: The defending champions, India, China and the US are Uzbekistan’s most dangerous rivals. India would have been the open Olympiad favourites but for the shaky form of the world champion, 20-year-old Gukesh Dommaraju, who was the top board gold medallist in Budapest two years ago but is likely to play lower down the order in Samarkand. USA are led by the world No 3 Fabiano Caruana and the world No 5 Wesley So, but their lower boards, including the variable Hans Niemann, look more vulnerable.

England, with an ageing squad, may struggle to reach the top 15, although they are seeded 12th. The oldest England player, nine-time British champion Michael Adams, is 54. Luke McShane is 42, Nikita Vitiugov and Gawain Jones are in their late 30s, while Daniel Fernandez, making his England debut, is 31. It is likely that the selectors would have chosen 17-year-old Shreyas Royal had they known that he would win the British championship, but that event was in August while Fide’s nomination deadline was in mid-July.

highlights.title: ‘Being Heumann’ Review: Siân Heder’s Drama About the Fight for Disability Rights Strikes Familiar Notes but Gets the Inspirational Uplift Job Done
highlights.summary: Ruth Madeley plays the leader of a milestone 1977 anti-discrimination protest, Judy Heumann, in Apple’s crowd-pleaser from the ‘CODA’ director, which opened the Toronto Film Festival.
body: In the first and best of many late ‘70s needle drops that punctuate Being Heumann, the punchy guitar groove of Iggy Pop’s “The Passenger” starts out over a close-up of wheels turning on pavement before the camera pulls back to take in disability rights activist Judy Heumann, maneuvering her wheelchair around crowded city streets and refusing to be intimidated even when a bus driver is bearing down on her with his hand clamped on the vehicle’s horn.

The first feature from director Siân Heder since her coming-of-age drama CODA went all the way from Sundance to a best picture win at the 2022 Oscars, Being Heumann follows a similar inspirational playbook, albeit lifted from a chapter in the American civil rights annals rather than drawing on real-life experiences to craft a fictional narrative. As with CODA, in which Heder cast deaf actors as deaf characters, the new film’s winning hand is the use of actors with disabilities to play the ragtag coalition led by Heumann in 1977 in what became the longest occupation of a federal building in U.S. history.

highlights.title: The Scoop With Nordic Poetry’s Ameli Lindgren: On a Rare Alexander McQueen Piece and Building an Archive
highlights.summary: This week’s guest is Ameli Lindgren, owner of Nordic Poetry, which, according to British Vogue, is one of the best vintage stores in the world and, according to my banking app, is where my son’s college tuition is being spent.
body: Welcome to The Scoop, a weekly email series in which I quiz fashion insiders on the stories of the week.

Nordic Poetry started as a small vintage market stall in 2007 and evolved into a vintage designer business in 2013, when Ameli secured a small store in London’s Boxpark Shoreditch mall. In 2017, she moved Nordic Poetry to Bethnal Green Road; it’s that store's pink walls you see in the background of all those Instagram Reels featuring Charli XCX, Gabbriette, and all their wedding guests trying on Tom Ford-era Gucci.

Ameli is currently working on Nordic Poetry’s fourth chapter, developing a curated fashion archive. I called her to get the scoop on that and to see if she has anything special prepared for London Fashion Week.

I wanted to kind of honor Seán McGirr’s first McQueen show in London with one of the rarest McQueen items in my archive. It’s this mask from Alexander McQueen’s Fall/Winter 1996 Dante collection, designed by Simon Costin. I believe only seven were made, and only two are circulating in the world right now. One is in LA, and the other is in our archive at Nordic Poetry. It’s an incredible piece of fashion history.
